name: Pentti Kanerva
org: UC Berkeley (Redwood Center for Theoretical Neuroscience)
subject: POLYDIM Framework: High-Dimensional Native Tensor Passing ($S^{D-1}$) & Hardware-Level Interop
body:
Dear Pentti Kanerva,

I have been following your work at UC Berkeley (Redwood Center for Theoretical Neuroscience) regarding Founder of Sparse Distributed Memory (SDM) & Hyperdimensional Computing.

At POLYDIM, we have been formalizing a paradigm for non-tokenized, continuous latent space communication between AI agents, operating directly on Riemannian hyperspherical manifolds (S^(D-1), D >= 10^4) with Clifford algebra rotors and zero-copy shared memory tensor passing (PMTP).

Key highlights:
- Eliminates the 1D text/JSON tokenization bottleneck across multi-agent pipelines.
- Preserves geometric entropy according to Data Processing Inequality (DPI).
- Sub-millisecond FFI execution with native CUDA C++20, Triton, and Rust Safe-SIMD kernels.

We would be honored to share our latest formal preprint and empirical benchmarks with you:
Empirical benchmarks and formal Clifford rotor proofs on S^(D-1)

Looking forward to your critical feedback and thoughts.

Best regards,

Ariel García Traba & Antigravity POLYDIM Team
Repository: https://github.com/tu-usuario/polydim
